messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert — HIGH p95 latency spike for hosted-api (us-west-2). Impact: generation endpoints showing 3-5x p95 increase. Triggered at 09:00 UTC. @Aisha you're on-call. :rotating_light:
Aisha: seeing it. opening thread. quick check — is this across all models or just the rtx-family?
Samir: looks like 98% of the requests hitting the vCPU-backed fallback router are fine, but GPU pool p95 jumps. maybe batching or KV cache pressure.
Aisha: running quick metrics: GPU latency graphs show tail rising starting ~08:55 UTC, concurrency steady. No config deploys in last 2 hours per deploy-bot.
Ellie: customer reports coming in (support) for slow responses. want a status page update?
Aisha: yes. triage steps: 1) confirm scope 2) mitigate (if possible) 3) update statuspage + customer comms 4) escalate to infra if needed.
Samir: repro check: hitting /v1/generate with model rtx-2048p causes streaming tokens delayed at token 1 for some requests. logs show RK cache misses spike.
Kai: might be cache thrashing after recent kernel change? But that's in dedicated runtime, not hosted — need process check.
Aisha: running quick process health on serving nodes in us-west-2: some worker pods show repeated OOMKilled during hot loops, restarts correlate with latency. attaching sample logs:
Aisha: ```
[2026-03-15T08:57:23Z] worker-12 ERROR: kv_cache_lookup timeout after 120ms
[2026-03-15T08:57:24Z] worker-12 INFO: triggering fallback to cpu-path
[2026-03-15T08:57:24Z] worker-12 WARN: memory pressure, evicting cache shard 3
```
Samir: that matches: cache eviction churn causing regen on GPU path, then fallback to slower path -> p95 spike.
Aisha: immediate mitigations we can try: a) increase cache memory on the affected node group b) temporarily route heavy customers to cpu-path with lower concurrency c) scale up GPU pool to absorb restarts. Thoughts?
Samir: we can bump kube memory request on the replica set (hot patch) and trigger a rolling restart of the affected nodes. doing a soft scale +1 on gpu-pool now.
Ellie: I'll draft status page message and a short customer notification. Keep it minimal: "We are investigating increased latency for hosted inference in US-West. Some requests may be slower; no data loss. Updates every 30m."
Aisha: good. Kai, can you kick off cache-mem bump and monitor? Also prepare an emergency rollback to prior runtime kernel if we see no improvement in 10m.
Kai: on it. Applying patch to kube manifest: `kubectl -n serving patch deployment gpu-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"6Gi"},"requests":{"memory":"4Gi"}}}]}}}}'`
Samir: I'm scaling the GPU autoset to +2 replicas now: `k8s scale deployment gpu-serving --replicas=12 -n serving`
Aisha: statuspage-bot, publish incident:component="Hosted Inference (US-West)" status="investigating" message="We are investigating increased generation latency impacting some hosted users in US-West. Token generation p95 elevated. Next update in 30 minutes."
statuspage-bot: Incident published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ri-2026-03-15-01
Aisha: Ellie, paste customer-facing blurb in support thread: short + what we're doing + ETA.
Ellie: customer-notice draft:
"Hi — we're seeing higher response times for some hosted inference requests in US-West. Our engineers have identified cache pressure on GPU nodes and are actively scaling and tuning caches. We expect improvements within 15-30 minutes; we'll follow up when fully resolved. No model outputs lost. — Redwood Ops"
Aisha: sending that to support to triage priority cases.
Kai: after memory bump some pods are stable, OOM events reduced. latency p95 down ~30% at 09:12 UTC. But still 1.8x above baseline.
Samir: rolling restart of worker set underway to clear bad state; rolling window 6m per pod.
Aisha: note for on-call: if latency doesn't drop to <1.2x baseline in next 20m, escalate to runtime team for kernel rollback. I'll be online for handoff.
Ellie: support update posted to customers, flagged tenants in us-west for high severity.
statuspage-bot: Updated incident ri-2026-03-15-01: status="monitoring" note="Mitigations applied: scaled GPU pool, increased cache memory, rolling restart. Latency improving; we continue to monitor. Next update in 30 minutes."
Aisha: current plan: continue to monitor, keep statuspage in monitoring, prepare rollback PR (Kai) but don't execute unless metrics plateau. Samir, keep scaling plan in place if restarts persist.
Kai: rollback PR ready: runtime/kernel@v1.12 -> v1.11. Holding until we hit escalation threshold.
Samir: two heavy tenants were auto-redirected to cpu-path to reduce load; that cut a bunch of load during restarts. Good emergency knob to keep.
Aisha: 09:35 UTC update: p95 back to 1.1x baseline. OOMs stopped. I'm going to mark this as resolved in 30m if stable. Preparing incident summary and internal comms template.
Aisha: internal summary draft:
"Short: transient p95 latency spike in us-west due to KV cache eviction + pod OOMs. Impact: increased token latency for some hosted-generation requests; no data loss. Mitigation: increased worker memory requests, scaled GPU pool +2, rolling restart, temporary routing of heavy tenants to CPU path. Recovery: p95 returned near baseline within ~35 minutes after mitigations. Action items: add early cache eviction alarms, tune memory requests for hot shards, postmortem to runtime kernel change."
Ellie: I'll sync with support to send final customer notif: short recap + link to status page + contacts.
Aisha: Kai, Samir — handoff to night oncall in 40m. I'll leave a sticky: monitor p95 for another 30m, escalate only if >1.3x baseline or new OOMs.
Samir: noted. I'll leave autoscale params in the runbook and enable the temporary cpu-redirect playbook for the night.
Aisha: thanks team. closing live thread; will update if anything changes.
statuspage-bot: Incident ri-2026-03-15-01 resolved at 10:05 UTC. Final note: "Mitigations successful; service restored to normal performance. A postmortem will be published."
